agenda_note: Authorization to award a contract to CTS Engineering, Inc. for an ADA Transition Plan in the amount of $268,555.00.
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}{\f1\fswiss\fprq2\fcharset0 Calibri;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced the item. He stated that this was the Authorization To Award A Contract for An ADA Transition Plan. \par
\par
\cf0 Jonathan Reinsvold, Village Engineer, stated Michael Melendez, Director of Business Development and Special Projects from CTS Engineering, Inc. was present and provided background information regarding the ADA Transition Plan. He showed an aerial of all of the neighborhood parks and community facilities. He said that this is for compliance with standards for community accessibility. He mentioned that the Request For Qualifications (RFQ) went out in June 2024; three firms submitted and the Selection Committee convened on July 30, 2024 and selected CTS Engineering. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone inquired about the scope and indicated he would like more clarity regarding the field work and reporting back to Council. \par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold explained the scope of work, data collection and evaluation using GIS based data application. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked what is the timeline.\par
\par
Mr. Melendez stated it is about 41 parks to be evaluated and discussed the schedule. \par
\par
Councilwoman Siskind asked about the Wellington Aquatic Center.\par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold answered a question from Councilwoman Siskind. \par
\par
Councilwoman Antu\'f1a asked if the plan is to go out and find deficiencies. \par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold answered a question from Councilwoman Antu\'f1a.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked if there is grant funding for this. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel spoke regarding grants. \par
\par
There was discussion regarding accreditation. \par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern asked if the parks were ADA compliant when they were initially built. \par
\par
Mr. Barnes discussed the parks and transition planning. \par
\par
Eric Juckett, Parks and Recreation Director, stated the Village needs to do this. \par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern asked what they would be looking for and asked for an example of what could be found. \par
\par
Mr. Melendez responded to Vice Mayor McGovern\rquote s question. \par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri mentioned Tiger Shark Cove and inquired what would be completed there.\par
\par
Mr. Melendez responded to Councilwoman Silvestri\rquote s question. \par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern asked what the training component would entail. \par
\par
Mr. Melendez responded to Vice Mayor McGovern\rquote s question. \par
\par
Mr. Barnes discussed the training aspect. \par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri asked if staff already knows how to perform this function. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone stated this seems to be a big amount for evaluation and asked if this is a bigger task than what Council thinks it is. \par
\par
Mr. Melendez briefly spoke about evaluation cycles and inspections. \par
\par
Mr. Juckett discussed Commission for Accreditation of Parks and Recreation Agencies (CAPRA) and the law. \par
\par
Mr. Barnes stated it is Federal law and ADA requirements. He said that it is a key requirement of CAPRA. \par
\par
Councilwoman Antu\'f1a asked about the manpower for this project. \par
\f1\fs22\par
\f0\fs24 Mr. De La Vega spoke regarding the manpower and hourly rates. \par
\par
There was further discussion regarding the engineer, cost and ADA compliance of the facilities.\cf1\par
}

agenda_note: Consideration and approval of the Purchase and Sale Agreement(s) for the sale of K Park to (a) Related Ross and (b) Education in Motion (EIM).
attachments: 1.  ACME_ Wellington K-Park - Purchase and Sale Agreement
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx810\tx841\tx2280\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced this item and provided brief background information. He stated representatives from Related Ross were present in the audience. Also, George Pincus (Stearns & Weaver/Village\rquote s Outside Counsel); Karen Yung, Education In Motion (EiM); and Frasier White (Chairman & CEO of EiM) were all appearing by Zoom.\par
\par
\pard\sa120\qj\cf0 Ms. Cohen said all of the parties and attorneys worked very hard on the Purchase and Sale Agreements (PSAs) and believe what has been presented to the Village Council is protective of the Village and the best agreement that staff was able to negotiate. She thanked all of the parties and attorneys for their hard work. \par
\par
Mr. Pincus provided a summary of the Related Ross and EiM PSAs in terms of purchase prices, due diligence, approvals and inspections periods, properties being sold \ldblquote as is/where is\rdblquote , termination rights, what is going to be developed at the properties, deed restrictions, zoning, deposits, and protections for what happens on the properties after their sold. \par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern asked Ms. Cohen to discuss the next steps in the process.\par
\par
Ms. Cohen stated this is the first step in a long process. She explained the next steps in the process regarding parcel re-plat, comprehensive plan amendment, rezoning of property and master plan, public participation/input, Council discussions, development order approvals, and closing on the property. She said the Council is only approving the PSAs tonight.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone mentioned the application process and public hearings and meetings. \par
\par
Ms. Cohen stated it would be no different than any other development application-it would follow the same process.\par
\par
Councilwoman Antu\'f1a asked if the contract is approved tonight, when would the contract be valid.\par
\par
Ms. Cohen stated it would be valid tonight but there are contract provisions that provide for other steps.\par
\par
Mr. Pincus outlined the Inspection and Approvals Periods. Closing is thirty days after the Approvals Period. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone stated the Village required a phased development for this project and this was important to the Village.\par
\par
Ms. Cohen referenced the Right of Repurchase Option. \par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern clarified that the repurchase options are at penalty to the applicant.\par
\par
There was discussion about the repurchase option and penalty that is included in both PSAs.\par
\par
Kenneth Himmel, President of Related Ross, highlighted their philosophy and commented that this is a mixed use project. He referenced what will be developed. He introduced Weber Hudson who has been the head of leasing of projects for Related all over the country.\par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern inquired about the Related Ross company and the vision.\par
\par
Mr. Himmel discussed Related Ross\rquote s succession plan and vision. He responded to the Village Council\rquote s questions in terms of density and type of hotel.\par
\par
Marianne Rehn, representing NewSchool Wellington, introduced her team members: Dr. Nicole Assisi, Strategic Academic Advisor, and Miles Graham, Financial Advisor to Frasier White and Karen Yung. She conducted a presentation regarding NewSchool Wellington and indicated it is a not-for-profit school.\par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern asked for clarification regarding whether the scholarships will be for Wellington residents only.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri stated she would like to see the scholarships be for Wellington residents only.\par
\par
Ms. Rehn responded to Council\rquote s questions regarding the lighting of the fields, ownership of the school and filing of documents for the operation of school.\par
\par
Mr. Kevin Ryan, Partner, spoke regarding the filing of documents for the school.\par
\par
Ms. Rehn stated the scholarships would be for residents only.\par
\par
Mr. White explained he and Ms. Yung could not attend in person due to family emergencies. He discussed their partnership with Related Ross and thanked the Council for their support. \par
\par
Ms. Yung expressed thanks to the Village Council for their leadership and support throughout the process and discussed their commitment towards building the school in Wellington.\par
\par
Vice Mayor McGovern asked what is the cost to build this school.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\ul\b Public Comment:\par
\pard\ulnone\b0\par
There were multiple public comments made in support and opposition to the project.\cf1\par
\par
\pard\sa120\qj\cf0 Mayor Napoleone gave comments regarding the project, school, dining options and landscaping and said options for this site have been talked about for ten years. He feels this is the best package with the best people behind it. He said he thinks this is a great project for Wellington and mentioned the traffic.\par
\par

\par

\par

agenda_note: Update on K-Park with Related Ross and ElevatEd.
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\fs24 Kenneth A. Himmel, President; Kevin A. Ryan, Executive Vice President/Development; and Maximillian Kaye, Project Manager/Special Projects were present from Related Ross. Marianne Rehn, President of ElevateED, was also in attendance. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan provided a brief overview of the progress that has been made regarding the project. He conducted a presentation regarding the existing site plan, reservoir pond, traffic mitigation issues, traffic signal, and the site plan for the Related Ross project. \par
\par
Mr. Himmel spoke regarding the retail, restaurant and hotel. He stated this will be a bespoke project for the Village. He referenced a fitness center and a private club.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan stated they have a professional office component and stated the spaces are fairly large. He stated they have moved into full schematic design. \par
\par
Mr. Himmel referenced the tenants and stated every space is designated to someone. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan showed some design precedents, reviewed the timeline summary and types of residences. \par
\par
Council asked questions regarding security, parking, dining, types of residences, rent amounts and whether golf carts will be allowed. \par
\par
Mr. Kaye referenced lighting and traffic calming features. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan mentioned the street systems and landscaping. \par
\par
Mr. Himmel stated they also invest in sculpture art for the project and will bring the Village into that process. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan stated there will be events programming, public spaces, second level uses. \par
\par
Mr. Himmel referenced the co-working space. \par
\par
Ms. Rehn, representing ElevateED, conducted a presentation about the progress for the private school. She mentioned the presentation she observed at the Education Committee meeting. She discussed the school investment, student population, school opening, Phase I and Phase II and the educational focus. Ms. Rehn presented a project progress update consisting of enrollment, program, design, permitting, approvals and costs. \par
\par
Council asked questions regarding the second phase (2031), students, amenities, exchange program, tuition costs, and programming for student athletes. \par
\par
Ms. Rehn stated there are three key areas of focus for the school: Entrepreneurship, Global Connections and Passion Ventures. She highlighted the learning environment, on-site medical and emergency care, mental health & well-being services, nutrition & physical activity and the environmental & holistic health approach. She also mentioned the architect and design team, state of the art learning spaces, sports facilities and a safe campus. Ms. Rehn pointed out features for architecture, technology and operations. She stated they will have a modern, safe electronic fleet for students to provide daily bus service. Lastly, Ms. Rehn provided a site plan design update. \par
\par
Council inquired about safety near the water and parent pickup/drop-off and school bus drop-off. \par
\par
Ms. Rehn reviewed the construction strategies and the detailed design update for the First Level, Second Level and Third Level as well as sports spaces. \par
\par
The Village Council gave comments regarding the update and the progress that had been made on the project.\par
\par
Ms. Rehn, Mr. Himmel and Mr. Ryan responded to Council comments and questions. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan stated they needed a Letter of Support from the Village to the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT). \par
\par
Mr. Barnes stated this will be brought forth to Council for approval.\cf1\par
}

\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced the item. He stated that this was the Budget Workshop and Ms. Quickel would begin the workshop presentation. He said that Jenoptik will provide a status presentation prior to the Agenda Review. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel said that this is the overall Governmental Capital Improvement Plan. She discussed the Capital Projects & Programs FY 2026 Funding. She said that the Village has $22 million capital projects and programs in this proposed Fiscal Year 2026 Budget. She said that there is $5.4 million for One Time Projects, $7.2 million for Ongoing Programs, and $9.2 for Utility Projects. She discussed the FY 2026 - FY 2030 Proposed Capital Improvement Plan. She said that as part of our planning, staff looks ahead an additional five (5) years, therefore FY 2027-2030. Ms. Quickel said that the major focus, as discussed at the April 25, 2025 Directions Workshop, is on Surface Water Management with the design of future pump stations supported by major grant applications with several pathway projects included. She indicated available funding is $1 million to 1.5 million per year from non-ad valorem assessments. Major grant applications for these projects are being submitted. \par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold discussed Pump Station #2 Rehabilitation. He said that the pump station design is complete and pending plan approval by FEMA along with the bid and procurement package. Staff expects procurement and construction to happen next fiscal year.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel said that the grant application process for Pump Station #2 was started in 2022; Phase I grant approval for the design portion was received two years ago. She mentioned the preliminary notice of approval in excess of $5 million funding for this. She said the process for this is extensive and Mr. Reinsvold and his team along with Mock Roos & Associates, Inc are working on everything to be compliant. Ms. Quickel stated we have not received the final documentation and agreement for Phase 2. She said they are looking at $38 million to $40 million as discussed at the Directions Workshop for the next five (5) to eight (8) years. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked if this is funded from the Utility Funds. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel said that these are mainly funded through FEMA, the Hazard Grant Mitigation Program, Resilience Florida and two new grant programs. \par
\par
Councilwoman Antu\'f1a asked about the number of Village grants. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel indicated that would be shown on an upcoming slide in the presentation. \par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold discussed the Pump Station Improvements for stations 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel mentioned the $650,000 awarded from the 2025 Legislative Appropriation for the Pump Station Improvement Project. \par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold discussed the Wellington Environmental Preserve Expansion, Road and Traffic Projects, Pathway & Trails Projects, Pathway & Bicycle Lane Projects, Lake Worth Rd & 120th Intersection, Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) & Vision Zero, and Capital Projects In Progress. \par
\par
There were comments and discussion regarding the roundabout.\par
\par
Councilman McGovern inquired about the opening dates for the Wellington Sports Academy.\par
\par
Mr. De La Vega responded to Councilman McGovern's inquiry. \par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri asked when the phases would begin for Streetscaping-Big Blue Trace.\par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold answered a question from Councilwoman Silvestri. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Siskind asked when is the tennis center expansion expected to be completed.\par
\par
Mr. Reinsvold answered a question from Vice Mayor Siskind.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel presented the FY 2026 Proposed Utilities Five Year Cap. She noted the overview outlining the fiscal year capital projects of approximately $9.2 million and said Ms. Panse would provide more detail in the Utility CIP Presentation.\par
}

\pard\nowidctlpar\ri-90\sa120\qj Douglas McMahon, CEO & Managing Partner/Wellington Lifestyle Partners (Applicant), thanked their team Miskel Backman LLP, Sexton Engineering, Simmons & White, and Cotleur Hearing. He provided brief overview and update about the project. \par
\par
Donaldson E. Hearing, Owner and President/Cotleur & Hearing (Agent), on behalf of the applicant, spoke about some of the technical aspects of the petitions (comprehensive plan amendment, conditional use and master plan amendment) before Council. He commented about the project context and history, project location and adjacencies, and showed Council a graphic of the existing and proposed future land use. Mr. Hearing referenced the Wellington PUD \endash Proposed Master Plan, Project Standards Manual, buffers for the site and proposed Marketplace Project Information. \par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri29\sa120\qj Mr. McMahon referenced the conceptual site plan and visuals of the project including offices, hotel, shops/restaurants and residences. He highlighted the uses, project connectivity and merchandising, positive financial impacts to the Village and circulation plan.\par
\par
Brian Kelly, P.E., Traffic Engineer/Simmons & White, briefly spoke about ongoing projects by WLP. He discussed the traffic review and analysis, parking & contingency plan, circulation plan - entrance and exit points, and Greenview Shores Boulevard exiting traffic. \par
\par
There was discussion between the Village Council, Ms. Cohen, Mr. Stillings, Mr. Kelly and Andrea Troutman (P.E., Founding Partner and President/Pinder Troutman Consulting, Inc.) about parking, traffic, the different types of uses, turn lanes, stacking, proportionate share contributions, previous approvals, peak hours, some changes to the language for the master plan amendment conditions (Condition 32A and Condition 32B regarding peak hours/times for the equestrian shows).\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj Ms. Ferraiolo reviewed the applicant\rquote s request and provided background information. Regarding the Comprehensive Plan Amendment (CPA), she showed a graphic of the current Future Land Use Map (FLUM) which shows the property as Commercial and the proposed FLUM that shows the property as Mixed-Use. She discussed the Conditional Use and Master Plan Amendment, staff analysis, and findings of fact. The Planning, Zoning and Adjustment Board (PZAB) recommended approval of all requests at their May 21, 2025 meeting. Council approved the CPA on first reading at the June 10, 2025 meeting. Ms. Ferraiolo discussed the additional conditions of approval that have been added to the Master Plan Resolution per Council discussion at the June meeting.\par
\par
The Village Council asked various questions about what could be built on the site currently without Council approval, timeframe of previous approvals, and conditions of approval.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri29\sa120\qj Mr. Stillings, Ms. Ferraiolo and Mr. McMahon responded to Council questions.\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx940\tx2379\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced this item.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\tx2160 Ms. Quickel indicated this is the first Public Hearing on the tentative millage and budget adoption for the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 budget. She said Wellington\rquote s budget process focuses on the Five Fundamentals: Neighborhood Renaissance, Economic Development, Protecting Our Investment, Responsive Government, and Respecting the Environment. She stated staff then developed the budget using insights and information from the 2025 Directions Workshop with the Village Council. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel highlighted the budget priorities: Deliver Essential Services Efficiently, Support Community Priorities, Fund Operations and Maintenance of Expanded Facilities while Minimizing Tax Impacts and Responsibly Invest in Wellington\rquote s Future.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Ms. Quickel stated the proposed budget is $155.9 million, which is $6.9 million more than the current year budget of $149 million She said this $6.9 million increase is primarily due to capital improvements, enhanced public safety and continued resident programs and services. She stated the proposed FY 2026 millage rate is 2.47 mills which has not changed from the current fiscal year. Ms. Quickel highlighted the proposed rates and assessments. She discussed the budget influences - revenues. She stated there is a range of tax impacts on various assessed values for both homesteaded and non-homesteaded properties. She referenced TRIM values and sample properties. Ms. Quickel discussed the change in Wellington values for actual properties from FY 2024 to FY 2025. She explained that 18.6% of the total tax bill goes to Wellington and Acme. Ms. Quickel discussed the General Fund and the FY 2026 Revenue Budget and Expenditures - All Funds. In addition, she provided the FY 2026 tentative budget adoption highlights. Ms. Quickel spoke about the expenditure budget influences and the FY 2025-2026 Budget Objectives.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel referenced the Budget Calendar and stated the second Public Hearing and final adoption will be held at the September 18, 2025 Council Meeting. She explained the advertising schedule. \par
\par
The Village Council made inquiries and provided comments regarding the millage, budget, services, reserves and funds. The Village Council commended Ms. Quickel and her team on the budget.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx810 Ms. Quickel responded to Council\rquote s questions.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Ms. Quickel read the mandatory language into the record.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Ms. Quickel acknowledged the departments, Ms. Wadleigh and Ms. Cabret for their work on the budget.\par
\par

\par
\ulnone\b A motion was made by Councilman McGovern, seconded by Vice Mayor Siskind, and unanimously passed (5-0), to open the Public Hearing.\par
\par

\par
\ulnone 1. Rick Christmas spoke regarding taxes, cell phone service, multi-modal pathways and shade covers in the parks.\par

agenda_note: Approval of the proposed Fiscal Year 2025-2026 millage rate, operating and capital budget including balances brought forward. This is the second public hearing on the proposed budget and the corresponding ad valorem millage rate in accordance with the Wellington Charter and F.S. Chapter 200.065.
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx940\tx2379\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced this item.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\tx2160 Ms. Hall read the Resolutions by title.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel indicated this is the second Public Hearing on the tentative millage and budget adoption for the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 budget. She said Wellington\rquote s budget process focuses on the Five Fundamentals: Neighborhood Renaissance, Economic Development, Protecting Our Investment, Responsive Government, and Respecting the Environment. She stated staff then developed the budget using insights and information from the 2025 Directions Workshop with the Village Council.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel highlighted the budget priorities: Deliver Essential Services Efficiently, Support Community Priorities, Fund Operations and Maintenance of Expanded Facilities while Minimizing Tax Impacts and Responsibly Invest in Wellington\rquote s Future.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Ms. Quickel stated the proposed budget is $155.9 million, which is $6.9 million more than the current year budget of $149 million She said this $6.9 million increase is primarily due to capital improvements, enhanced public safety and continued resident programs and services. She referenced the methods for FY 2025-2026 Budget Public Engagement. She stated the proposed FY 2026 millage rate is 2.47 mills which has not changed from the current fiscal year. It is the average from the past seventeen years. She stated there is a range of tax impacts on various assessed values for both homesteaded and non-homesteaded properties. Ms. Quickel discussed the General Fund and the FY 2026 Revenue Budget and Expenditures - All Funds. In addition, she explained that 18% of the total tax bill goes to Wellington. She highlighted Spending versus Property Tax and What Ad Valorem Taxes Buy for the General Fund. Ms. Quickel discussed the FY 2026 Budget Adoption and the FY 2025-2026 Budget Objectives. She also discussed a Wellington Grants Summary and Largest Revenue Sources for the Village.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Ms. Quickel acknowledged the Village Council, Mr. Barnes, Mr. De La Vega, Ms. Christine Wadleigh, Ms. Ana Acevedo, Ms. Rubi Cabret and Mr. Jeff Gomez and the departments for their work on the budget.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\ul Public Hearing\par
\par
\ulnone\b A motion was made by Councilman McGovern, seconded by Vice Mayor Siskind, and unanimously passed (5-0), to open the Public Hearing.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx810 There being no public comments, a motion was made by Councilman McGovern, seconded by Vice Mayor Siskind, and unanimously passed (5-0), to close the Public Hearing.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160\b0 The Village Council commended Ms. Quickel, her team, the departments and the residents for their work, efforts and participation in the budget process.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160\b A motion was made by Councilman McGovern, seconded by Vice Mayor Siskind, and unanimously passed (5-0), to approve Resolution No. R2025-64 (Millage Rate) adopting the tax levy and millage rate for the Village of Wellington for the fiscal year commencing October 1, 2025 at 2.47 mills.\par
\par
A motion was made by Councilman McGovern, seconded by Vice Mayor Siskind, and unanimously passed (5-0), to approve Resolution No. R2025-65 (Wellington Budget)\b0 \b adopting the budget for the Village of Wellington for FY 2025/2026.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa240\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160\b0 Ms. Quickel read the mandatory language into the record.\par
\pard\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes said that there are two items as it relates to the Palm Beach County Code of Ethics. He stated that there are two Advisory Board Members that are affected by this particular code provision, and the requirement is to provide the disclosure to Council at a public meeting, which what is being done now. He said Tatiana Yaques, CEO of CCTV Agent P.B. Inc, is a member on the Planning, Zoning and Adjustment Board. He noted that the Village had done business with that company prior to Ms. Yaques' acquisition and involvement with the firm. He said that the total value to date is approximately $11,000. He said that Stephen Levin, Principle of the Western Ride, LLC, is a member of the Parks and Recreation Advisory Board, which the Village had partnered with and that event was recently held. He said that it is a not-for-profit that benefits Donna's Fund, which is for Women In Distress Broward County. He mentioned that Mr. Levin had come before the Council on multiple of occasions to discuss that project; however, there was not a specific disclosure that may not have met the requirements of the Code; staff is disclosing that now. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch stated the reason that this disclosure is being made is because there is an exception for the provision of the Code of Ethics for Advisory Board members. If the board that they are on does not provide oversight or regulation of the contract at issue, then the disclosure can be made a public meeting, and that does not violate the Code of Ethics. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented on the disclosure. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch responded to Mayor Napoleone's comment. \par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced the item. He stated that this was the K Park Update Presentation WIth Related Ross. He stated that the Related Ross Team is present.\par
\par
Kenneth Himmel, President Related Ross, introduced the team and new players Jorge Mendoza, Senior Vice President of Design at Related Ross, Webber Hudson, Executive Vice President, Retail Leasing and Asset Management Related Ross, and Katie Block, Chief Financial Officer Related Ross. He said that David Manfredi will be presenting some of our latest work here tonight. He discussed the restaurateurs and bringing a higher level hotel concept. He thanked the Council for making the right choice selecting Related Ross. \par
\par
Mr. Manfredi presented the PowerPoint Presentation Wellington Village Project. He said that the goal is to make a downtown that is absolutely walkable with mixed uses, the pedestrian is primary, making a neighborhood, and open space. He discussed the Conceptual Site Plan. \par
\par
Councilman McGovern asked how many right turns would be on Stribling Way. \par
\par
Kevin Ryan, Executive Vice President/Development Related Ross, answered a question from Councilman McGovern. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Siskind commented on the traffic on Stribling Way. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan responded to Vice Mayor Siskind's comment. \par
\par
Mr. Manfredi continued presenting the Conceptual Site Plan, Concept - Wellington Village Project and Concept - Hotel. \par
\par
Mr. Himmel noted a major fitness and health club across from the hotel. He said that there is a commitment for a 35,000 square foot user but the name cannot be revealed yet.\par
\par
Councilman McGovern asked is this in both of the locations. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan answered a question from Councilman McGovern. \par
\par
Councilman McGovern asked if the hotel would connect to the event space.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan answered a question from Councilman McGovern. \par
\par
Councilwoman Antu\'f1a asked if the hotel will be the highest building in the development.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan answered a question from Councilwoman Antu\'f1a.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked if there is any kind of rooftop amenity on the hotel. \par
\par
Mr. Manfredi, Mr. Ryan and Mr. Himmel responded to Council comments and questions. \par
\par
Mr. Webber presented the Site Merchandising Plan. He said there is something for everybody. He stated that we have been in the market and have talked to a couple hundred retailers and have 18 letters of intent that are actively engaged. He said that we will be announcing those in the first quarter of next year. \par
\par
Councilman McGovern inquired if we are going to be able to announce tenants the first quarter of 2026. \par
\par
Mr. Webber and Mr. Himmel responded to Councilman McGovern's inquiry. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan discussed the Project Schedule Summary. He thanked Mr. Barnes and the entire staff for working very hard and very collaboratively with us on the approvals process. He stated that the site work is set to start March 2026; with target open date for October 2028. He discussed the Offsite Improvements Diagram. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Siskind commented regarding the previous traffic studies done. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan responded to Vice Mayor Siskind's comment. He spoke regarding Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) condition of approval. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan discussed the RR Development Future Expansion. \par
\par
Councilman McGovern asked if the amount parking will stay the same or go up.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan and Mr. Himmel answered a question from Councilman McGovern. \par
\par
There were comments and discussion regarding the mix use and designs. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked what is the arrangement with the church on shared parking.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan and Mr. Himmel answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Mr. Ryan said that they have been speaking with staff about a Community Development Districts ( CDD) that we are exploring. He said that the Village would have to approve and endorse. He said it is a vehicle to typically use tax exempt bonds to fund infrastructure and improvement. He said that we would work with staff to explain that in more detail at other meetings.\par
\par
Councilman McGovern asked what is the timeline for this. \par
\par
There was comments and discussion regarding the CDD, appropriations and funding.\par
\par
Maximillian Kaye, Project Manager/Related Companies stated that we are still exploring the exact vehicle. He said ultimately the Village of Wellington would be the applicant, there would be no money put up from the Village side. It would be state and private funding. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented you are hoping to come with a State appropriation with a match from your side.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan and Mr. Himmel responded Mayor Napoleone's comment. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked how does the timing of this work with your schedule.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan and Mr. Kaye answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Councilman McGovern asked how does this change or line-up with the appropriations that the Village is already seeking.\par
\par
Mr. Barnes answered a question from Councilman McGovern.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented that we do not want to risk our appropriation. \par
\par
Mr. Barnes responded to Mayor Napoleone's comment. \par
\par
Councilman McGovern asked about Purchase and Sale Amendments Environmental concerns.\par
\par
Mr. Ryan answered a question from Councilman McGovern. He said that we are heading towards putting up and additional deposit on November 21, 2025. \par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri commented everything is absolutely beautiful and she looks forward to moving forward this with this. \par
\par
Mr. Himmel thanked the Village for their support.\par
}

agenda_note: Update from the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser’s Office for tax year 2026.
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Jackson thanked the Village Council for having him. He said that Dorothy Jacks Palm Beach County Property Appraiser apologies for not being present, she is out of town. He said he would present the latest market trends and some of the taxable values for Wellington and how values change over time, breakdown by property types and what it means for the tax base going forward. He presented the PowerPoint Presentation The Village of Wellington. He said Wellington taxable value increased from about $12.4 billon in 2024 to just over $13.2 billion in 2025 which is about at 6.62 percent increase which is in line with the County growth that grew about 8 percent. The net new construction in Wellington is more that $57 million dollars in taxable value in 2025 which is roughly about $5.5 billion County wide. He said that 62.4 percent of Wellington's properties are homestead, County wide is 56.1 percent so you see a strong home base here in Wellington. He said that Wellington continues to see a solid taxable growth and supports both the appreciation and the construction. He discussed the Wellington 2025 values by property type.He said the residential properties are parcels by far the most numerous with close to 19,000 parcels, the non residential classifications such as the commercial industrial properties are fewer in number but each represents a substantial amount of value, especially on the taxable side, the agriculture parcels care about several billion in market value. He said that the taxable value column represents how much of the market values actually available to support services after the exemptions and limits right in classifications. The table highlights abroad, diverse mix of property type supporting Wellingtons physical position going in the 2025. It is a very strong base compared to a lot of other municipalities in Palm Beach County. He discussed the Market Value and Taxable Values.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked why the market value is higher that the taxable value. \par
\par
Mr. Jackson answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Councilman Levin asked Mr. Jackson to characterize the vacant as the definitions in the documents show that vacant is really property that is due to be transferred, not necessarily property with no structure on it.\par
\par
Mr. Jackson answered question from Councilman Levin. He continued and discussed how the state law and local classifications can shift the burden of property types. He presented the 2017-2025 market & Taxable Values Wellington. He said that we do not have the 2026 numbers, the numbers will probably come out late May for all the cities in the County. He said that roughly about 18,000 to 21,000 properties sell in the County-wide each year, we verify that this property is an arms links transaction that people know that when we are putting out values for properties we are actually supporting that with what we see in terms of the market. He said that the net new construction was about $85 million in taxable value; our total taxable value countywide is $5.8 billion last year. We are looking at $78 million dollars for the 2026 Tax Roll, we are down almost $5 million in value from last year but it still $73 million in new taxable value that would be added to the your assessments. He said that there is a lot of demolitions but there is a lot of new added value. Single family residential construction increased and rose about $27 million dollars from $25million to $45 million dollars, the agricultural has gone in the opposite direction decreasing from about $41 million in 2025 to about $28 million dollars. He mentioned the Lotis Wellington plat has approximately about $23 million in market value. He said that the PBC Appraiser is keeping an eye on the property tax legislation. He noted that Mr. Manitos has sent over a link for the Power Bi Dashboards of those proposals for House Bills 201, 203 and 205 are still on the dashboard showing the impacts on how that would effect the VIllage of Wellington if property taxes were eliminated and the County as a whole.All the proposals would not eliminate school taxes, Fire or Police as they would still have to be funded. House Bill 201 Elimination of Non-school Property Tax for Homesteads; was sponsored by Representative Steele. He said that there would be a $12.9 million dollar reduction in revenue to the Village of Wellington, House Bill 205 Elimination of Non-School Property Tax for Homesteads for Persons Age 65 or Older, this would be a $5.2 million dollar reduction in revenue; and House Bill 209 Property Insurance Relief Homestead Exemption Non-school Property Tax, the properties would get an extra $100,000 deduction in taxable value minus the non school property taxes reducing the tax bills for the County. The homeowner must have a qualified insurance policy and requires verification. If this was applies this would be an elimination of about $2.9 million dollars in revenue almost $3 million dollars. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked if the $100,000 increase the homestead cap from $50,000 to $100,000 if you have homeowners insurance. \par
\par
Mr. Jackson answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked if any bills came out of the Senate. \par
\par
Mr. Jackson answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a asked if any of three bills taking the lead at this moment.\par
\line Mr. Jackson answered a question from Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a.\par
\par
Councilman Meier asked if any other states had any strategies to overcome those deltas in dollars or any strategies that they have talked about. \par
\par
Mr. Jackson answered a question from Councilman Meier.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented on the talks about sales tax increase. \par
\par
Mr. Jackson responded to Mayor Napoleone's comment.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel noted link in the agenda item summary with the dashboard for the various bills to see the calculations discussed for the Village of Wellington and various cities.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked if the link could be sent again. \par
\par
Mr. Jackson answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. He thanked the Village for allowing him to come and speak.\par
\par
\par
}

minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced the item. He stated that this is the E-Bikes and Micro Mobility Discussion.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch presented the item. She presented the PowerPoint Presentation "Micro Mobility Devices in Wellington". She discussed What is a Micro Mobility Device?, General Rule, Municipalities Can, Proposed Ordinances, Chapter 22 - Traffic and Vehicles, and Chapter 14 - Parks.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented on the speed limits on designated multimodal pathways.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch responded to Mayor Napoleone's comment. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a commented if e-bikes and e-scooters are not allowed on the sidewalks they will go onto the road.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch responded to Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a's comment.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented that human powered bicycles are allowed on sidewalks; what the Village is proposing is that an electric powered vehicle is not allowed on the sidewalk. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch answered a question Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Ms. Coates said that golf carts are not regulated within gated communities on private property. What the Village is proposing would not apply to private roadways and gated communities. \par
\par
Mr. Barnes said that the Village has some private communities that have private roads that are not gated, it would be dependent upon that community's HOA as to what they permit inside those communities. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a asked would this apply inside HOAs.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch answered a question from Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri commented that the biggest issue is when kids are going to the middle schools and coming home. If the Village had some deputies stationed during those times, there would not be a need to do this. She asked if there is a plan for enforcement. \par
\par
Sergeant James Benedict, Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, responded to Councilwoman Silvestri's comment.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri asked what is the school police authority regarding this issue. \par
\par
Assistant Chief of Police Michael Waites, Palm Beach County School District, answered a question from Councilwoman Silvestri. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked Assistant Chief Waites what does a mutual aid agreement look like.\par
\par
Assistant Chief Waites and Sergeant Benedict answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Councilman Meier asked if e-motos fall under the same enforcement. \par
\par
Sergeant Benedict provided a brief overview of e-motos and enforcement. \par
\par
Councilman Meier asked can micro mobility be limited or excluded on the bridle paths. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch answered a question from Councilman Meier.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri asked if the bridal paths includes golf carts as well.\par
\par
Mr. Barnes and Ms. Bausch answered a question from Councilwoman Silvestri. \par
\par
There were comments and discussion regarding mopeds and e-motos on the bridle trails. \par
\par
Councilman Meier asked if the speed limit of 15 miles per hour was only allowed on multi modal pathways but they are they allowed to go faster than that on the street. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch and Sergeant Benedict answered questions from Councilman Meier. \par
\par
Councilman Meier commented that if the Village is able to make the restriction as far as the age limit of who can ride these things, would it be a good idea to make the age limit 16. He inquired how PBSO would know if someone is 15 years old, 16 years old or 14 years old. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented that he is not a fan of the age limit.\par
\par
There were comments and discussion regarding e-bikes, e-scooters and golf carts on equestrian trails.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone and Sergeant Benedict answered question from Councilman Meier. \par
\par
There were comments and discussion regarding the age, requiring government issued IDs, enforcement and speed limits. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a commented the Village needs to pick the priorities as this is very important. She does not like the age restriction. \par
\par
Ms. Cohen said that it would be beneficial to hear from PBSO as to what their top concerns are. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch continued and discussed enforcement. She said that the enforcement under the proposed ordinance would be done by PBSO. She said it is a non-criminal traffic infraction and punishable as a pedestrian violation pursuant to Chapter 318. It is a pretty low fine amount in the amount of $15. If enforced as a Uniform Traffic Citation (UTC), meaning it is a violation of State Law; there are certain associated fees.\par
\par
Deputy Michael Maniscalco said the fee is $64.50 after the Clerk of Court receives their fees. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch said if this is enforced as a violation of the Village Ordinance to be determined to exactly what is going to be punished in the ordinance; it would still be the $15. Staff is still working on the what the additional fees would be. Staff needs to confer with the Palm Beach County Clerk of Court because that would be done separate from PBSO. She said Chapter 22 refers you to Chapter 14. She noted the proposed change to Chapter 22 that addresses the enforcement of the golf cart violations. \par
\par
There were comments and discussion on the civil penalty. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked if the Village wants to set a flat fee of $100.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch said staff wants to set a flat fee of non-moving $116 and moving around $166 with court cost. She continued and presented Chapter 14-Parks. She noted the areas where property damage has occurred.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri asked if they can pull up to the parking lot or put them over to the side.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch answered a question from Councilwoman Silvestri. \par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri asked if there is a designated area now for them to park their scooters at all of the different parks and if there is signage. \par
\par
Mr. Barnes and Ms. Bausch answered a question from Councilwoman Silvestri.\par
\par
Ms. Coates said that the current signs state no scooters, bicycles, roller blading or skateboards; those signs would be updated. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch discussed the subsection in Chapter 14 that deals with the use of vehicles in parks to address e-bikes and e-scooters. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked what does it mean by not at Wellington Town Center.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch and Mr. Barnes answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch continued and said that Chapter 14 clarifies that the section can be enforced by law enforcement, in addition to park staff. It clarifies the penalty for Chapter 14 as a whole is consistent with what is in Florida Statute Chapter 162. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented that he is good with Chapter 14, he has no issue.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri commented that she is fine with Chapter 14.\par
\par
Councilman Meier commented he is wondering if anything is being left out. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone commented that a lot of his concerns are addressed with the State Statutes. The only section he would take out is Section 22-48 the age restriction. He would suggest updates to the section that would allow e-bikes and motorized scooters where bikes are allowed. \par
\par
Ms. Cohen asked Mayor Napoleone if he has an issue with Section 22-48 Government issued ID.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone answered a question from Ms. Cohen. \par
\par
Sergeant Benedict commented that he is fine with a school issued ID. \par
\par
Councilman Meier said he is stuck on the age restriction. He relayed his concern regarding safety and the age restriction. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a asked if the parents are notified when they get a citation or no citation. \par
\par
Sergeant Benedict answered a question from Vice Mayor Antu\'f1a,\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked Ms. Bausch what happens if a kid gets a citation and it is not paid.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch, Deputy Maniscalco and Ms. Cohen answered a question from Mayor Napoleone. \par
\par

attachments: 1. 2026-17 Amendment to Chapter 14 (Micro-mobility Devices in Wellington Parks) 7.17.26.docx
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced the item. He stated that this was the Ordinance No. 2026-17 (Operation of Non-Human Powered Micro-Mobility Devices). \par
\par
Ms. Bausch presented the item. She said this is the first reading of the ordinances discussed at the July 16, 2026 Workshop. She said this addresses the changes to the Parks Chapter, which is Chapter 14, and with respect to what was discussed at the workshop, nothing has changed in that section. This is the section that is going to clarify that e-bikes, e-scooters and e-skateboards and anything electric is also not allowed in those park locations where bicycles and scooters are already prohibited. It also adds references to playground equipment, boat ramps, and neighborhood parks, which are places the Village has experienced property damage. The other changes to that section are to have specific requirements in relation to non-human-powered micromobility devices, which is the new definition that was added based on the direction from the workshop. She said that Ordinance No. 2026-16 makes changes to Chapter 22, which is Traffic and Vehicles. The golf cart penalty is being modified to make it a fixed amount as opposed to the gradual penalty that it is now. Additionally, staff created some regulations for micromobility devices, where the definition of non-human-powered devices was added. The regulations for those devices are that a photo ID is required to be carried while you operate it. A school ID is acceptable for minors. The speed limit on sidewalks and pathways is 15 miles per hour, and devices are prohibited from being used on public bridal trails. She said, based on the direction that was given at the workshop, the Village is not imposing an age restriction; there is no restriction limiting them on multimodal pathways. Therefore, sidewalks and pathways are fine.\par
\par
Councilman Levin asked does a non-human powered micro mobility device include electric wheelchairs or scooters. \par
\par
Ms. Bausch answered a question from Councilman Levin. \par
\par
There was comments and discussion regarding the definition of non-human powered devices.\par
}

minutes_note:

{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\expndtw-2\fs24 This item formerly Public Hearing Item 8B.\par
\par
\pard\ri-14\sa120\qj\expndtw0 Mr. Barnes introduced this item. He stated that there would be one combined public hearing with two separate motions since the Ordinances are going to be considered at the same time. \par
\par
Mr. Barnes read Ordinance No. 2026-16, Ordinance No. 2026-17 and Resolution No. R2026-42 by title.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch stated that these are two separate ordinances addressing micromobility devices and this is the second reading for both ordinances. She discussed Ordinance No. 2026-16 and Ordinance No. 2016-17. She summarized what was approved on first reading and referenced the supplement that was provided to Council regarding the changes that had been made from first reading to second reading. \par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\tx2160 Council asked questions regarding the age component, identification, parks and parking lots.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch responded to Council\rquote s questions.\par
\par
\ul Public Hearing\par
\par
\ulnone\b A motion was made by Councilwoman Silvestri, seconded by Councilman Meier, and unanimously passed (5-0) to open the public hearing.\par
\ul\b0 Public Comment:\par
\par
\ulnone 1. Scott Harper spoke regarding the micromobility ordinance and said he does not agree with the age limit. He suggested a rider education program.\par
\par
2. Ben Brown spoke regarding ebikes, emotos and the micromobility ordinances. He inquired about helmet language.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch stated the ordinance does not address helmet use because helmet use because it is already the law under Florida Statutes. It would be a statutory violation.\par
\par
3. Lauren Brody spoke about the ordinances and said no bicycles of any kind belong on a sidewalk. She expressed her concerns and suggestions regarding ebikes, sidewalks, multimodal paths and education. \par
\par
4. Elizabeth Pandich said with the Winter Equestrian Festival or any horse show that takes place there are USCF rules regarding motorized vehicles for kids under 16. She spoke about helmets.\par
\par
5. Bruce Tumin spoke about ordinance changes, helmets, public safety, local authority, and rate of speed. He suggested the ordinance be tabled.\par
\par
6. Jim Summers spoke about the safety of other residents using the sidewalks in pathways. He said he has almost been hit multiple times and feels the devices are dangerous.\par
\par
7. Jennifer Mayfield read a letter into record from her daughter regarding e-scooters. Her best friend, Mia Moore, was also present at the podium.\par
\par
\b There being no further public comments, a motion was made by Councilman Levin, seconded by Councilwoman Silvestri, and unanimously passed (5-0) to close the public hearing.\par
\par
\b0 Council thanked those who attended the meeting for coming. There was further Council discussion regarding an education component, age restriction, safety, rules, enforcement, helmet requirement, state law, fines, incidences with walkers/runners, golf carts, identification and multi-modal pathways.\par
\par
Ms. Bausch responded to Council\rquote s questions.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa240\qj\tx839\tx2280\b\par
A motion was made by Councilwoman Silvestri, seconded by Councilman Meier, and passed (3-2; Mayor Napoleone and Councilman Levin dissenting) to approve Ordinance No. 2026-16 (Penalty For Golf Cart Violations And Operation Of Micro-Mobility Devices On Public \expndtw-2 Rights-Of-Way) \expndtw0 as amended to include the ID change, the age limitation and the helmet reference with state law on second reading.\b0\par
\pard\cf1\par
}

agenda_note: Council tentative approval of the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 proposed millage rate of 2.47 mills and the proposed operating and capital budget including balances brought forward. This is the first public hearing on the proposed budget and the corresponding ad valorem millage rate in accordance with the Wellington Charter and Florida Statutes Chapter 200.065. The second public hearing and adoption is to be held on September 22, 2026.
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\ri43\sa120\qj\tx980\tx2419\cf1\fs24 This Item formerly Item 6C.\par
\par
Mr. Barnes introduced the item.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\tx2160 Ms. Quickel indicated this is the first Public Hearing on the tentative millage and budget adoption for the Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 budget. She said Wellington\rquote s budget process focuses on the Five Fundamentals: Neighborhood Renaissance, Economic Development, Protecting Our Investment, Responsive Government, and Respecting the Environment. She stated staff then developed the budget using insights and information from the 2026 Directions Workshop with the Village Council. \par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\tx2160 Ms. Quickel highlighted the budget priorities: Deliver Essential Services Efficiently, Support Community Priorities to Enhance Quality of Life, Fund Operations and Maintenance of Facilities to Maximize Use and Responsibly Invest in Wellington Innovation and Safety.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Ms. Quickel stated the total proposed FY 2027 budget is $150.4 million, which is $5.5 million less than the current year budget of $155.9 million. She said this $5.5 million decrease is primarily due to reduced capital improvements, elimination of positions, leasing of major equipment and no election expense. She stated the proposed FY 2027 millage rate is 2.47 mills which has not changed from the current fiscal year. She highlighted the proposed rates and assessments and FY 2026-2027 TRIM Millage Rates Comparison. She discussed the budget influences - revenues. Ms. Quickel stated there is a range of tax impacts on various assessed values for both homesteaded and non-homesteaded properties. She referenced TRIM values and sample properties. She discussed the change in Wellington values for actual properties from FY 2025 to FY 2026. Ms. Quickel explained that 18.7% of the total tax bill goes to Wellington and Acme. She discussed the FY 2027 Revenue Budget - All Funds and the FY 2027 Expenditures - All Funds. She spoke about the General Fund - Spending vs. Property Tax and What Ad Valorem Taxes Buy. In addition, she provided the FY 2027 tentative budget adoption highlights. Ms. Quickel spoke about the expenditure budget influences and the FY 2026-2027 Budget Objectives.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel referenced the Budget Calendar and stated the second Public Hearing and final adoption will be held at the September 22, 2026 Council Meeting. She explained the advertising schedule. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel reviewed the largest revenue sources for the Village, how some of that money is spent, and the FY 2026-2027 Budget Cuts. She said the proposed FY 2026-2027 Budget is presented with an overall decrease of $7.81 million in the governmental funds.\par
\par
The Village Council commended Ms. Quickel and her team on the budget.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\ul Public Hearing\par
\par
\ulnone\b A motion was made by Councilwoman Silvestri, seconded by Councilman Meier, and unanimously passed (5-0), to open the Public Hearing.\par
\par
\pard\sa120\qj\cf0\ul\b0 Public Comment:\par
\par
\ulnone 1. Bruce Tumin spoke regarding capital improvements and budget.\par
\par
2. Ivan Stevens inquired about Village investments.\par
\pard\li720\sa120\qj\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx810\cf1\b There being no further public comments, a motion was made by Councilwoman Silvestri, seconded by Councilman Meier, and unanimously passed (5-0), to close the Public Hearing.\par
\par
\b0 The Village Council made inquiries and provided comments regarding the millage, budget, positions, services, rollback rate, budget cuts, possible revenue streams and reserves.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx810 Mr. Barnes and Ms. Quickel responded to Council\rquote s questions.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Mayor Napoleone passed the gavel to Vice Mayor \cf0 Antu\'f1a\cf1 .\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri86\sa120\qj\tx810\b A motion was made by Mayor Napoleone, seconded by Councilman Levin, and passed (4-1; Councilman Meier dissenting) to approve the proposed FY 2027 millage rate, budget and adoption of the Fiscal Year 2026/2027 Capital Improvement Plan on first public hearing.\par

agenda_note: Approval of the proposed Fiscal Year 2026-2027 millage rate, operating and capital budget including balances brought forward. This is the second public hearing on the proposed budget and the corresponding ad valorem millage rate in accordance with the Wellington Charter and F.S. Chapter 200.06.
attachments: 2 - FY 2027 MIllage Resolution No. R2026-49 2.47 mills
3 - FY 2027 Budget Adoption Resolution No. R2026-50 2.47 mills
minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\ri43\sa120\qj\tx980\tx2419\cf1\fs24 Mr. Barnes introduced the item.\par
\par
Ms. Hall read Resolution No. R2026-49 and Resolution No. R2026-50 by title.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\tx2160 Ms. Quickel indicated this is the second Public Hearing on the tentative millage and budget adoption for the Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 budget. She said Wellington\rquote s budget process focuses on the Five Fundamentals: Neighborhood Renaissance, Economic Development, Protecting Our Investment, Responsive Government, and Respecting the Environment. She stated staff then developed the budget using insights and information from the 2026 Directions Workshop with the Village Council. \par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\tx2160 Ms. Quickel highlighted the budget priorities: Fund Operations and Maintenance of Expanded Facilities While Minimizing Tax Impacts, Responsibly Invest in Wellington\rquote s Innovation and Safety, Deliver Essential Services Efficiently, and Support Community Priorities.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx29\tx720\tx2160 Ms. Quickel stated the total proposed FY 2027 budget is $150.4 million, across all funds and was tentatively adopted on the first public hearing. The budget shows an overall reduction of $5.5 million less than the current year\rquote s total budget. She said this $5.5 million decrease is primarily due to reduced capital improvements, elimination of positions, leasing of major equipment and no election expense. She stated this budget funds all recurring operations and rising fixed costs with no change in the millage rate. She reviewed the FY 2027 Total Budget - All Funds, FY 2026-2027 Budget Public Engagement, Proposed Rates; and stated 2.47 mills is proposed. Ms. Quickel provided comments about resiliency focused budgeting and discussed the FY 2027 Revenue Budget - All Funds and the FY 2027 Expenditures - All Funds. She spoke about the millage rate impacts and the FY 2026-2027 Millage Rate Decision. Ms. Quickel explained that 18.7% of the total tax bill goes to Wellington and Acme. In addition, she reviewed the General Fund - Spending vs. Property Tax and showed a sample tax bill. She spoke about the General Fund-What Ad Valorem Taxes Buy and the FY 2027 final budget adoption highlights. \par
\par
Ms. Quickel said the proposed FY 2026-2027 Budget is presented with an overall decrease of $7.81 million in the governmental funds. Ms. Quickel reviewed the FY 2026-2027 Budget Cuts. She also provided the Wellington Grants Summary, largest revenue sources for the Village and the expenditures provided by those revenue sources. Ms. Quickel thanked the Village Council, Mr. Barnes, Mr. De La Vega, Ms. Fischer, Ms. Acevedo, Ms. Cabret and the departments.\par
\par
The Village Council commended Ms. Quickel and her team on the budget.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\sa120\qj\tx29\tx840\ul Public Hearing\par
\par
\ulnone\b A motion was made by Councilwoman Silvestri, seconded by Councilman Meier, and unanimously passed (5-0), to open the Public Hearing.\par
\par
\pard\sa120\qj\cf0\ul\b0 Public Comment:\par
\par
\ulnone 1. Lauren Brody spoke about the budget and what is paid for by the residents. She suggested establishing a finance committee.\par
\par
2. Bruce Tumin spoke regarding items and expenditures in the budget.\par
\par
3. Laurene Capone expressed her concerns about the budget and expenditures.\par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\ri90\sa120\qj\tx810\cf1\b There being no further public comments, a motion was made by Councilman Levin, seconded by Councilwoman Silvestri, and unanimously passed (5-0), to close the Public Hearing.\par
\par
\b0 Councilman Meier provided comments and proposed a 2.40 millage rate.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri asked Ms. Quickel to relay the suggestions discussed in their meeting.\par
\par
Ms. Quickel relayed the budget suggestions.\par
\par
Councilwoman Silvestri spoke briefly about other suggestions for the budget and proposed a 2.45 millage rate.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone inquired about the 10 percent pertaining to insurance.\par
\par
Councilman Levin inquired about the insurance and thanked Ms. Quickel and her team for their efforts with the budget. He spoke about grants and the millage rate.\par
\par
Vice Mayor \cf0 Antu\'f1a\cf1 referenced the budget cuts, millage rate, reserves and Amendment 3. She commended staff for their work on the budget.\par
\par
Mayor Napoleone asked Mr. Barnes to explain the cumulative impact of a millage rate reduction overtime and on an annual basis.\par
\par
Mr. Barnes discussed the calculation regarding a roll back rate, millage rate majority and supermajority vote, and changes made the past legislative session. \par
\par
Mayor Napoleone stated the millage rate has been held at 2.47 and that rate funds what the residents enjoy. He mentioned Amendment 3 and budget expenditures. The Mayor suggested keeping the 2.47 millage rate for this year and charge staff to review lowering the millage rate for next year.\par
\par
There was further discussion between the Village Council and staff regarding the millage rate, budget cuts, possible revenue streams and reserves.\par
\par
